paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks. The vertical axis on the left side represents the accuracy as a percentage, with a linear scale ranging from 40% to 65%, marked with tick labels at 5% intervals. The horizontal axis contains categories for different models or methods, although it is not explicitly labeled. There are six bars, each representing a different model or approach: RoBERTa w/o Exp. in gray, ExEnt in light blue, LaSQuE (mean) in orange, LaSQuE in green, LaSQuE (syn2real) in purple, and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) in dark gray. The approximate accuracy values are 47% for RoBERTa w/o Exp., 55% for ExEnt, 47% for LaSQuE (mean), 47% for LaSQuE, 60% for LaSQuE (syn2real), and 62% for LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum), with the bars for LaSQuE (mean) and LaSQuE being of equal height and the bars not sorted in any specific order, and no bars are visually emphasized.
